info.name: Sabame API
info.description: Sabame's current HTTP API. Main requests use baseUrl (http://localhost:3000) through Next.js. backendUrl (http://localhost:4000) is for direct NestJS diagnostics only. Complete MAL OAuth in a browser; account routes use the sabame_mal_session cookie. Examples are illustrative, not captured. No credentials or cookie values are included. Source ownership: NestJS routes are in apps/api/src/modules, playback routes are in apps/web/src/app/api, and Next.js rewrites are in apps/web/src/config/backend-routing.ts.

item.name: health
item.description: Health and readiness checks. These requests use the frontend origin by default. Change the request host to backendUrl only when diagnosing Nest directly.

request.description: Returns process status without checking PostgreSQL. Response: 200 with status ok. This request can also reach Nest directly at backendUrl for diagnostics.

Checks database connectivity with SELECT 1 and queries the account table. Response: 200 with status ready, or 503 with status unavailable. Readiness does not check migration drift or upstream providers.

item.name: auth
item.description: Session, logout, and MyAnimeList OAuth routes. The app uses the sabame_mal_session HttpOnly cookie. Postman does not complete MAL consent or extract browser cookies.

request.description: Returns { configured, user }. A signed-in session includes the MAL user id, name, and optional picture. Without a session, user is null. This read does not require Origin or a JSON body. Errors include 503 database_not_configured or database_unavailable when account storage cannot be used.

Starts the interactive browser login. Open this URL in a browser at appOrigin. Sabame returns 303 to MAL and sets a short-lived HttpOnly sabame_mal_oauth transaction cookie. Complete consent in the browser so MAL returns to /api/auth/mal/callback on the same origin. Do not run this as an automated Postman login. Misconfiguration and origin errors redirect to /login?mal_error=... rather than returning a JSON error.

response.name: Illustrative 303 redirect to login on configuration failure

query.description: One-time code supplied by MAL. Browser flow only.
OAuth state supplied by MAL. Browser flow only.
Optional OAuth denial value supplied by MAL.

request.description: Browser callback for MAL OAuth. MAL supplies code and state, and the browser sends the transaction cookie set by Start MAL OAuth. On success, Sabame exchanges the code, sets sabame_mal_session, clears the transaction cookie, and redirects to /dashboard. On failure, it redirects to /login?mal_error=.... Do not call this request manually; its one-time query values and cookie come from the browser flow.

Revokes the current session when its cookie is present, then clears sabame_mal_session. Send Origin exactly equal to appOrigin and Content-Type application/json. The JSON body is parsed but ignored, so {} is sufficient. The request uses a session cookie from Postman's local cookie jar if one is present. Errors include invalid_origin 403, invalid_request 400 or 413, and database errors 503.

response.name: Illustrative 403 wrong origin

item.name: catalog
item.description: Public anime search, seasonal browsing, detail, and episode metadata. These GET requests do not require a session cookie.

query.description: Search text. Use 2 to 100 characters for a provider lookup.

request.description: Query parameter q is trimmed. A query shorter than 2 characters or longer than 100 returns { results: [] } with 200. Otherwise results contains up to 20 non-adult anime records using the shared Anime fields. Upstream metadata errors can return a 502 error envelope; a 504 indicates timeout.

query.description: Optional page number from 1 through 100. Defaults to 1.

request.description: Required query parameters: year and season. Year must be an integer from 1917 through the current year plus one. Season is winter, spring, summer, or fall. Page is optional and defaults to 1; when supplied, it must be an integer from 1 through 100. Returns { items, nextPage }; nextPage is null when there is no later page. Invalid input returns 400 invalid_request.

Returns one Anime record for an MAL id such as mal-123, or a supported seeded catalog id. The Anime shape includes id, title, subtitle, synopsis, genres, totalEpisodes, episodeMinutes, accent, and optional score or image URLs. Errors include 404 anime_not_found, 409 mapping_required, and 502 metadata or upstream failures.

Returns { episodes }, where each item has a positive number and title. The catalog uses provider streaming episode metadata when present, then falls back to numbered episodes from the episode count. Errors include 404 anime_not_found, 409 mapping_required, and 502 metadata or upstream failures.

item.name: library
item.description: MAL account library reads and writes. Private routes require sabame_mal_session. Every JSON write requires Origin exactly equal to appOrigin and Content-Type application/json.

query.description: Optional opaque nextCursor from the previous page. Leave disabled for the first page.

request.description: Requires a signed-in session cookie. The first page omits cursor. Each page contains at most 50 items and 50 operations. Follow nextCursor as an opaque continuation until it is absent; do not edit or decode it. A cursor is account-scoped and tied to a library revision. If the revision changes between pages, the server returns 409 library_changed. Invalid or cross-account cursors return 400 invalid_request.

response.name: Illustrative 409 stale cursor

request.description: Requires sabame_mal_session and a successful import-capable MAL connection. Send Origin equal to appOrigin, Content-Type application/json, and { expectedUserId } matching the current session user id. Returns the first library page after import. Common errors include 401 unauthorized, 403 invalid_origin, 409 account_changed or sync_busy, 503 mal_unavailable, 503 storage or configuration errors, and 504 import_timeout. The import replaces the local snapshot with the current MAL list.

response.name: Illustrative 409 account changed
Illustrative 504 import timeout

request.description: Requires sabame_mal_session. Send Origin equal to appOrigin and Content-Type application/json. animeId must match mal-[1-9] followed by up to 7 digits. The body requires expectedUserId, a stable operationId of 16 to 100 letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens, base, and a non-empty changes object. base is the last known MAL status object or null when the anime was absent. changes may contain watchedEpisodes as a safe integer from 0 through 10000 and/or status from watching, planned, completed, on_hold, or dropped. Keep operationId, base, and changes unchanged when retrying the same action. A changed payload with a reused operationId returns 409 operation_mismatch. A conflicting remote edit returns 409 with operation.state conflict and operation.remote. To resolve, resend the same operation with resolution local to apply your changes, or resolution remote to accept the remote state. A failed upstream update can return 200 with operation.state failed; inspect operation.error.

response.name: Illustrative 200 tracking operation synced
Illustrative 409 operation id reused with different input

item.name: schedule
item.description: Personalized broadcast schedule. Requires a signed-in session and an imported MAL list. The response is filtered to anime in the user's list.

query.description: Valid ISO week number for year.
IANA time zone, such as Asia/Bangkok.

request.description: Required query parameters: year, week, tz, and airType. year is from 2000 through 2100; week must be a valid ISO week for that year; tz must be a supported IANA time zone no longer than 64 characters; airType is all, sub, dub, or raw. Requires sabame_mal_session and an imported list. Returns { state: ready, season, matchedAnimeCount, items }. An imported list with no matched titles returns an empty items array. Errors include 401 unauthorized, 400 invalid_request, 409 list_not_imported, 502 upstream_unavailable, 503 not_configured, and 504 timeout.

response.name: Illustrative 200 personalized schedule
response.body:
{

item.name: playback
item.description: Next.js playback routes. Resolve a source, then use only its short-lived signed resource URL. The resource endpoint does not serve unauthenticated plaintext streams.

request.description: Resolves one episode through Next.js. Send Content-Type application/json and { episodeNumber }, an integer from 1 through 10000. If Origin is present, it must match the request URL origin. The response is MediaResult with provider, video, subtitles, metadata, thaiStatus, and selectionReason. Video and available subtitle URLs point to /api/media/resource with short-lived signed tickets. Common errors include 400 invalid_request, 404 anime_not_found, no_source, or episode_unavailable, 409 mapping_required, 502 upstream_unavailable, and 504 timeout. This route does not require a MAL session.

header.description: Optional MP4 byte range, capped at 8 MiB.

query.description: Short-lived signed capability from the media resolution response.

request.description: Requires the ticket query parameter returned by Resolve Episode Media. A ticket is a short-lived signed bearer capability; keep it local and do not share it. Tickets expire within 30 minutes and are checked against an HTTPS host allowlist. The server fetches the resource only after ticket verification. The response may be a subtitle, HLS manifest, or media bytes depending on the signed ticket. For MP4, Range accepts one bytes start-end range and each request is capped at 8 MiB; without Range, the first 8 MiB is requested. There is no unauthenticated plaintext stream. Common errors include 403 invalid_ticket, 410 source_expired, 502 upstream or invalid range failures, and 504 timeout.

variable.description: Frontend origin used for normal requests through Next.js.
Direct NestJS origin for diagnostics only.
Exact frontend origin sent on JSON writes.
Set locally to the signed-in MAL user id.
Set locally to an anime id such as mal-123.
Set locally to a stable id of 16 to 100 allowed characters.
Set locally to a short-lived signed media ticket.
